access_failures.result: Web fetch rejected content larger than 4 MB; overview not counted as read. Focused command pages used.
Two web fetches returned internal errors; XCLAIM documentation used for recovery contract. No XAUTOCLAIM-specific claims adopted.

claim_corrections.correction: Buffering changes acceptance and durability; it is not an automatic cure for database saturation.
Command acknowledgement, recovered delivery and committed external effects are distinct.
Stream length, consumer-group progress and server replication progress measure different things.
Primary routing and replication/fsync waits do not establish strong consistency through async failover.
Prefix broadcasting can increase invalidation fanout.
Routing distribution and mutable-copy coherence need separate evidence.
Eviction eligibility must follow acceptable loss, not a universal TTL policy.
Threading and per-command complexity matter; there is no universal few-thousand-members cutoff.
Removal visibility and background memory reclamation are separate observations.

practice_cards.trigger: Move mutations from synchronous database commits to Redis-buffered processing.
practice_cards.failure: An accepted request disappears before the database effect, or a lost reply causes a second enqueue/effect.
practice_cards.mechanism: Define the acceptance boundary, allowed loss window, persistence/failover configuration and recovery evidence. Preserve an application operation ID through uncertain replies.
practice_cards.conditions: Inspect actual server/client support and same-connection WAIT/WAITAOF result counts. A timeout does not establish that the earlier write failed.
practice_cards.counterexample: Disposable telemetry may accept loss; a financial mutation cannot silently inherit that policy. Synchronous database writes do not universally require replacement.
practice_cards.verification: Proposed: interrupt after enqueue and after persistence-wait timeout; restart under the chosen configuration and reconcile accepted IDs against committed effects.
practice_cards.inference: Acceptance policy and identity reconciliation are application requirements derived from command boundaries.

practice_cards.trigger: Redis work is consumed into a separate database.
practice_cards.failure: Destructive pop or premature ACK loses work; commit-before-ACK duplicates effects; trimming or overload destroys replay inputs.
practice_cards.mechanism: Use recoverable pending ownership, stable scoped identity, transactional effect/outcome recording and ACK after commit. Bound admission, batches and worker concurrency; track oldest unfinished work and queue bytes.
practice_cards.conditions: Reclaiming ownership does not fence external writes. Retain payload and deduplication state for supported recovery; inspect trimming policy and poison-work disposition.
practice_cards.counterexample: A processing list alone cannot deduplicate a bank API call. Unbounded buffering only postpones a sustained capacity deficit.
practice_cards.verification: Proposed: lose ACK after commit, resume an old worker after reclaim, stop consumers until admission limits activate, then replay retained work.
practice_cards.inference: Database transaction, admission and external-effect fencing requirements are derived application design.

practice_cards.trigger: High write rates invalidate many local cache entries.
practice_cards.failure: BCAST amplifies matching-prefix traffic; lost invalidations permit stale local reads.
practice_cards.mechanism: Compare selective/default tracking and BCAST using actual subscriptions, mutation rate and hit savings. On uncertain tracking continuity, invalidate or bypass affected local state until tracking is re-established.
practice_cards.conditions: Check protocol/client reconnect handling. Narrow prefixes exclude unrelated keys but every subscriber still receives matching changes.
practice_cards.counterexample: A write-heavy prefix subscribed by all clients can make BCAST more expensive than selective caching.
practice_cards.verification: Proposed: compare two clients that read disjoint keys, update an unread matching key, then disconnect invalidation delivery and check the declared freshness fallback.
practice_cards.inference: Local-cache recovery policy and comparative workload measurements are recommendations, not built-in guarantees.

practice_cards.trigger: Replica routing must satisfy freshness or read-your-writes across services.
practice_cards.failure: Stream cardinality or health timestamps are mistaken for applied database state; failover loses required history.
practice_cards.mechanism: Separate XLEN, group pending/lag, and replication ID/offset. Compare offsets only within compatible replication history; require application freshness evidence or an explicit bounded fallback.
practice_cards.conditions: Offsets count replication bytes, not elapsed freshness. Last interaction is a health signal. Primary routing remains subject to acknowledgement and failover semantics.
practice_cards.counterexample: A fully retained stream can have high XLEN after all effects finish; zero group lag can coexist with pending work.
practice_cards.verification: Proposed: pause replication and a consumer independently; record each metric, then exercise required-revision reads and a history-changing failover.
practice_cards.inference: An application revision/fallback protocol is additional design, not a property conferred by a metric.

practice_cards.trigger: One key dominates command time or network traffic.
practice_cards.failure: Randomly selected mutable copies diverge or remain on the same resource.
practice_cards.mechanism: Measure the bottleneck and actual slot/node placement. Prefer bounded payload/access patterns; consider immutable version-addressed copies only with an explicit publication/read contract.
practice_cards.conditions: Mutable copies require partial-update, deletion and delayed-fill recovery. Shared hash tags can colocate copies; cross-slot atomic operations are restricted.
practice_cards.counterexample: Copying one value ten times on a standalone server does not create ten servers. A partitioned counter is a different aggregation contract.
practice_cards.verification: Proposed: interrupt a copy update, race a stale fill with deletion and record the selected copy/version; verify slot placement separately.
practice_cards.inference: Copy coherence hazards and immutable-version alternative are deductions from distribution/atomicity boundaries, not a vendor recipe.

practice_cards.failure: A lock, ordering floor or deduplication record is removed before its required retention boundary.
practice_cards.mechanism: Classify disposable values versus correctness state. Choose eligible loss explicitly, isolate roles where appropriate and define behavior for missing metadata or rejected writes.
practice_cards.conditions: Volatile policies select TTL-bearing keys; no eligible keys means noeviction-like rejection. Protecting a key from eviction does not establish restart durability.
practice_cards.counterexample: Adding TTL to every key makes critical metadata eligible; removing all TTLs merely to avoid eviction changes expiration semantics.
practice_cards.verification: Proposed: force early eviction under the chosen policy; assert metadata loss takes the supported recovery/failure path and overload cannot grow without bound.
practice_cards.inference: Early-loss safety and state-role separation apply documented policy eligibility to application invariants.

practice_cards.trigger: Large values, maintenance or deletion correlate with foreground latency.
practice_cards.failure: Member-count folklore misses expensive replies; deferred free backlog is mistaken for instantaneous memory recovery.
practice_cards.mechanism: Budget command and reply bytes, batch sizes and concurrency from representative measurements. Consider UNLINK for costly aggregate disposal and inspect lazy-free progress separately from RSS. Bound pipeline request/reply bytes; batching alone is not transactional.
practice_cards.conditions: I/O/background threads do not remove ordinary command head-of-line blocking. A large batch still has per-key work; allocator retention can keep RSS high.
practice_cards.counterexample: One field lookup in a large hash differs from returning the whole hash; a small collection of huge values can still saturate the network.
practice_cards.verification: Proposed: compare bounded field reads and whole-object reads while measuring unrelated-request latency; check immediate key absence and later reclamation separately.
practice_cards.inference: Workload budgets require measurement; no throughput or latency gain is asserted here.
